# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));
  `PlanSegment.path` (the clip alone when absent) and `origin` (nil) read a nested audio
  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and
  `gates` a gated clip's hide-while-silent gate (format 43, spec §11 CO-93). `AudioProps.swift`

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

== get_media_analysis
{"required": ["kind"], "addl": null}
  media {"type": "integer"} :: The media whose picture or sound to analyse — exactly one of media and clip.
  kind {"type": "string", "enum": ["shots", "masks", "faces", "sound_events", "subjects"]} :: What to find: shots, the hard cuts; masks, a person's masks' runs; faces, every face per sample (box, roll, yaw, mouth); sound_events, laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech per window of sound; subjects, people and salient regions per sample.
  from {"type": "integer"} :: Where to start, in the media's SOURCE ticks (the file played forwards, 600000 per second), not snapped: 0, or the clip's played window's start, by default.
  to {"type": "integer"} :: Where to stop (not included), in the media's SOURCE ticks: the media's end, or the clip's played window's end, by default; must be after from.
  project {"type": "string"} :: Path of the open project to act on, as get_project reports it; omit for the frontmost one.
  clip {"type": "integer"} :: A media clip: its media analysed over the part the clip plays — exactly one of media and clip.
== get_timeline_transcript
{"required": [], "addl": null}
  to {"type": "integer"} :: Where on the TIMELINE to stop reading, in ticks, snapped to frames; the timeline's end by default. Must be after from.
  tracks {"items": {"type": "integer"}, "type": "array"} :: Only the words playing on these timeline tracks (ids from get_project); every track by default.
  language {"type": "string"} :: A language tag, e.g. en-US, for this Mac's recogniser only (a cached transcript answers in its own language). This Mac's own language by default; each language is kept apart in the cache. A tag speech recognition does not know is refused with the tags it knows, and one whose on-device model is not installed is refused as not installed — this tool never downloads.
  project {"type": "string"} :: Path of the open project to act on, as get_project reports it; omit for the frontmost one.
  from {"type": "integer"} :: Where on the TIMELINE to start reading, in ticks (600000 per second), snapped to frames; the timeline's start by default. A word across this edge comes back whole.
== analyze_cutout
{"required": [], "addl": null}
  project {"type": "string"} :: Path of the open project to act on, as get_project reports it; omit for the frontmost one.
  wait {"type": "number"} :: How many seconds to wait for every clip to settle, 0 to 60; 0 (answer now) when left out.
  clips {"items": {"type": "integer"}, "type": "array"} :: The cut-out clips to answer for; every cut-out clip in the open scope, in timeline order, when left out.
== relay_captions
{"required": [], "addl": null}
  project {"type": "string"} :: Path of the open project to act on, as get_project reports it; omit for the frontmost one.
== import_captions
{"required": ["path"], "addl": null}
  project {"type": "string"} :: Path of the open project to act on, as get_project reports it; omit for the frontmost one.
  path {"type": "string"} :: Absolute or ~ path to the .srt file.
  track {"type": "integer"} :: Put the captions on this existing track instead of a new one. Cues the overlap rule refuses there are dropped, so prefer omitting it.
== transcribe
{"required": [], "addl": null}
  style {"enum": ["subtitles", "highlight", "pill", "karaoke", "build", "one_word"], "type": "string"} :: subtitles (default: two-line cues in the Caption preset, unchanged) or a word caption style that shows each word as it is said: highlight (Montserrat Black, upper case, the word in yellow with a pop), pill (Montserrat ExtraBold, upper case, the word on a violet pill), karaoke (Montserrat ExtraBold as written, up to two lines, words turning yellow), build (Anton, upper case, words appearing one by one) or one_word (Bebas Neue, one large word at a time). Anything else is refused with the six named. A style is a display choice: a cached transcript is reused whatever style is asked for, and restyling is running transcribe again with replace.
  vocabulary {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}} :: engine "assemblyai" only. Words and phrases to expect — product names, people, identifiers. Trimmed, de-duplicated keeping the first spelling, and capped at 1000 terms with the cap named in note. Refused by name with engine "apple".
  slide {"type": "boolean"} :: The pill slides from the word before to the word being said, over 0.2 s or sooner, instead of jumping: writes word_style.active_pill.glide true on every page placed. Default false, and never what the sheet last chose. It applies with style pill: true is refused by name with any other style or with place false, where it would show nothing; false is always accepted (unlike replace, which is refused whenever it is given where it cannot apply).
  language {"type": "string"} :: A language tag, e.g. en-US. WITH apple: this Mac's own language by default. The two ways a tag can be wrong are two different problems with two different fixes, so they are refused SEPARATELY and the message says which you have. A tag speech recognition has never heard of is a misspelling: it is refused with the tags it does know. A tag it knows whose on-device MODEL is not installed on this Mac is refused as not installed, with the languages ready here: a person has to install it from the Generate Captions sheet, and this tool never downloads. WITH assemblyai: "auto" (the default) detects it and the result reports what was detected and how sure it was; a code is passed through unchecked, and one AssemblyAI does not support comes back as its own sentence after the upload.
  clips {"type": "array", "minItems": 1, "items": {"type": "integer"}} :: Transcribe only these clips — the sheet's scope. Omit for every clip in the project that has recorded sound. Only a clip playing a movie or sound file can be transcribed, and not one played in REVERSE, whose words would come out backwards; a clip you name that cannot be is reported under skipped.
  project {"type": "string"} :: Path of the open project to act on, as get_project reports it; omit for the frontmost one.
  refresh {"type": "boolean"} :: engine "assemblyai" only. Ignore the cached transcript and upload again (default false). Refused by name with engine "apple", which has no cache.
  place {"type": "boolean"} :: Place the cues as text clips (default true), as ONE undo step. false returns the cues and changes nothing at all — no edit, no undo step — which is the way to check a transcript before committing to it.
  speakers {"type": "boolean"} :: engine "assemblyai" only. Ask for speaker labels (default false); a change of speaker then starts a new cue, and with style subtitles each speaker's cues take their own colour (white, yellow, cyan, green in order of first appearance, then again; a speaker is a label within one media file). Refused by name with engine "apple".
  dim {"type": "boolean"} :: The page fades to half its opacity in a pause of 0.25 s or more: writes word_style.pause_dim 0.5 on every page placed. On-device (engine apple) words rarely carry a pause that long, so it shows mostly with assemblyai. Default false, and never what the sheet last chose. It applies with style highlight, pill, karaoke, build or one_word: true is refused by name with any other style or with place false, where it would show nothing; false is always accepted (unlike replace, which is refused whenever it is given where it cannot apply).
  replace {"type": "boolean"} :: With a word style and place true only — refused by name with subtitles or with place false. true removes, in the SAME undo step, every caption track this command could have made over these clips: named Captions or Captions N, holding only text clips, each of which overlaps a clip being transcribed. The result lists them under replaced.
  engine {"type": "string", "enum": ["apple", "assemblyai"]} :: Where the recognition happens: apple (default) on this Mac, assemblyai in the cloud. Anything else is refused with both spellings named. The default is NEVER what the sheet last chose — an agent that wants the cloud says so every time.
  fill {"type": "boolean"} :: The word being said fills left to right as it is spoken, taking 0.6 s at most: writes word_style.active_fill true on every page placed. Default false, and never what the sheet last chose. It applies with style highlight, karaoke or build: true is refused by name with any other style or with place false, where it would show nothing; false is always accepted (unlike replace, which is refused whenever it is given where it cannot apply).

{"required": ["clip"], "addl": null}
  language {"type": "string"} :: A language tag, e.g. en-US, for this Mac's recogniser only (a cached transcript answers in its own language, reported as language). Matched as transcribe matches it: this Mac's own language by default; a tag speech recognition has never heard of is refused with the tags it knows, and one whose on-device model is not installed is refused as not installed — a person installs it, this tool never downloads.

  to {"type": "integer"} :: Where on the TIMELINE to stop reading, in ticks (600000 per second), snapped to frames; the clip's end by default. Must be after from. A word across this edge comes back whole, with its own times.

== transcribe
{"required": [], "addl": null}
  style {"enum": ["subtitles", "highlight", "pill", "karaoke", "build", "one_word"], "type": "string"} :: subtitles (default: two-line cues in the Caption preset, unchanged) or a word caption style that shows each word as it is said: highlight (Montserrat Black, upper case, the word in yellow with a pop), pill (Montserrat ExtraBold, upper case, the word on a violet pill), karaoke (Montserrat ExtraBold as written, up to two lines, words turning yellow), build (Anton, upper case, words appearing one by one) or one_word (Bebas Neue, one large word at a time). Anything else is refused with the six named. A style is a display choice: a cached transcript is reused whatever style is asked for, and restyling is running transcribe again with replace.
  vocabulary {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}} :: engine "assemblyai" only. Words and phrases to expect — product names, people, identifiers. Trimmed, de-duplicated keeping the first spelling, and capped at 1000 terms with the cap named in note. Refused by name with engine "apple".
  slide {"type": "boolean"} :: The pill slides from the word before to the word being said, over 0.2 s or sooner, instead of jumping: writes word_style.active_pill.glide true on every page placed. Default false, and never what the sheet last chose. It applies with style pill: true is refused by name with any other style or with place false, where it would show nothing; false is always accepted (unlike replace, which is refused whenever it is given where it cannot apply).
  language {"type": "string"} :: A language tag, e.g. en-US. WITH apple: this Mac's own language by default. The two ways a tag can be wrong are two different problems with two different fixes, so they are refused SEPARATELY and the message says which you have. A tag speech recognition has never heard of is a misspelling: it is refused with the tags it does know. A tag it knows whose on-device MODEL is not installed on this Mac is refused as not installed, with the languages ready here: a person has to install it from the Generate Captions sheet, and this tool never downloads. WITH assemblyai: "auto" (the default) detects it and the result reports what was detected and how sure it was; a code is passed through unchecked, and one AssemblyAI does not support comes back as its own sentence after the upload.
  clips {"type": "array", "minItems": 1, "items": {"type": "integer"}} :: Transcribe only these clips — the sheet's scope. Omit for every clip in the project that has recorded sound. Only a clip playing a movie or sound file can be transcribed, and not one played in REVERSE, whose words would come out backwards; a clip you name that cannot be is reported under skipped.
  project {"type": "string"} :: Path of the open project to act on, as get_project reports it; omit for the frontmost one.
  refresh {"type": "boolean"} :: engine "assemblyai" only. Ignore the cached transcript and upload again (default false). Refused by name with engine "apple", which has no cache.
  place {"type": "boolean"} :: Place the cues as text clips (default true), as ONE undo step. false returns the cues and changes nothing at all — no edit, no undo step — which is the way to check a transcript before committing to it.
  speakers {"type": "boolean"} :: engine "assemblyai" only. Ask for speaker labels (default false); a change of speaker then starts a new cue, and with style subtitles each speaker's cues take their own colour (white, yellow, cyan, green in order of first appearance, then again; a speaker is a label within one media file). Refused by name with engine "apple".
  dim {"type": "boolean"} :: The page fades to half its opacity in a pause of 0.25 s or more: writes word_style.pause_dim 0.5 on every page placed. On-device (engine apple) words rarely carry a pause that long, so it shows mostly with assemblyai. Default false, and never what the sheet last chose. It applies with style highlight, pill, karaoke, build or one_word: true is refused by name with any other style or with place false, where it would show nothing; false is always accepted (unlike replace, which is refused whenever it is given where it cannot apply).
  replace {"type": "boolean"} :: With a word style and place true only — refused by name with subtitles or with place false. true removes, in the SAME undo step, every caption track this command could have made over these clips: named Captions or Captions N, holding only text clips, each of which overlaps a clip being transcribed. The result lists them under replaced.
  engine {"type": "string", "enum": ["apple", "assemblyai"]} :: Where the recognition happens: apple (default) on this Mac, assemblyai in the cloud. Anything else is refused with both spellings named. The default is NEVER what the sheet last chose — an agent that wants the cloud says so every time.
  fill {"type": "boolean"} :: The word being said fills left to right as it is spoken, taking 0.6 s at most: writes word_style.active_fill true on every page placed. Default false, and never what the sheet last chose. It applies with style highlight, karaoke or build: true is refused by name with any other style or with place false, where it would show nothing; false is always accepted (unlike replace, which is refused whenever it is given where it cannot apply).

#!/usr/bin/env node
// A fast check of pages, in about a second, with no site build:
//
//     node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs [page.mdx …]      # all pages when none is named
//
// Each page must parse (frontmatter and MDX), name a title and a description, import every
// component it uses, link only to pages in the sidebar, and name only captures that exist.
// `pnpm build` is still the last word: it also checks that every link's #anchor exists.

import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, relative } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { compile } from '@mdx-js/mdx';
import remarkGfm from 'remark-gfm';
import { parse } from 'yaml';
import { sidebar } from '../sidebar.mjs';

const SITE = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
const CONTENT = join(SITE, 'src/content/docs');
const SCREENS = join(SITE, 'src/assets/screens');
const COMPONENTS =
  /<(Steps|Aside|Tabs|TabItem|Card|CardGrid|LinkCard|LinkButton|Badge|FileTree|Icon|AtAGlance|Shot|FeatureIndex)\b/g;

function slugs(items, found = new Set(['', 'features'])) {
  for (const item of items) {
    if (typeof item === 'string') found.add(item);
    else if (item.slug) found.add(item.slug);
    else if (item.items) slugs(item.items, found);
  }
  return found;
}

function pages(folder, found = []) {
  for (const entry of readdirSync(folder)) {
    const path = join(folder, entry);
    if (statSync(path).isDirectory()) pages(path, found);
    else if (/\.mdx?$/.test(entry)) found.push(path);
  }
  return found;
}

content.content:
[What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/) says exactly what leaves your Mac and how it's deleted. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) covers the rest of the sheet.

## The price before you press Generate

The summary line prices the run at AssemblyAI's published rate, and updates as you change a control:

`2 files to upload · 01:12:30.000 of audio · about $0.25 at AssemblyAI's published rate · 1 file already transcribed`

The rate is $0.21 an hour of audio, plus $0.02 an hour with **Speakers:** on. Those are the figures AssemblyAI published on 2026-09-17. They're built into Frame Job and aren't fetched, so AssemblyAI's own bill is the real figure. Each file is priced at its whole length, because AssemblyAI [bills for the whole file](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-is-uploaded-and-billed).

A very short run reads "under $0.01". When every file is already transcribed the line starts "Nothing to upload", as in `Nothing to upload · 2 files already transcribed`.

Two more counts can appear, and neither is in the price:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "1 file waiting on an earlier delete" | The file [isn't uploaded](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#a-pending-delete-holds-a-file-back) until AssemblyAI confirms an earlier delete. |
| "1 file could not be read" | Frame Job couldn't read the media file, so it can't be transcribed. With nothing else to do, **Generate** is greyed. |

## Why each file uploads

Rest the pointer on the summary line. You get one line for each file that isn't already transcribed, saying why, and then the rate as a dated sentence.

| The line says | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| "has not been transcribed yet" | This file has no transcript in the project. |
| "has changed since it was transcribed" | The file on disk isn't the one that was transcribed. |
| "was transcribed with a different language" | The named setting differs from the transcript's. It can also name **model**, **speakers** or **vocabulary**, or several of them. |
| "was transcribed for a different request" | Something else about the request differs. |
| "is already transcribed, and Transcribe again was asked for" | You ticked [Transcribe again](#transcribe-again). |
| "could not be read, so it cannot be transcribed" | The media file couldn't be read. |

## Split the words by speaker

Tick **Speakers:** ("split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles") to have AssemblyAI label who says what. It's off by default and adds $0.02 an hour to the price.

A change of speaker then always starts a new cue or page. In the [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) style, each speaker's cues take their own colour.

Speakers are counted separately for each media file. A speaker is a label within one file, so the same person in two files can come back as two different speakers.

## Add names and jargon

Type the words you expect into **Vocabulary:**, separated by commas: product names, people, identifiers. AssemblyAI then spells them your way. The field starts empty, and its placeholder reads "names and jargon, separated by commas".

Blank entries and repeats are dropped, keeping the first spelling. The list stops at 1,000 terms, which is AssemblyAI's limit, and it's cut from the end, so put the terms that matter most first. When the limit cuts your list, the note reads "Vocabulary was capped at 1000 terms (AssemblyAI's limit); N were given."

## Choose a language

**Language:** opens on **Detect automatically**, which leaves the language to AssemblyAI. The [result](#what-the-result-says) then tells you what it found.

You can also name one: English, English (Australia), English (United Kingdom), English (United States), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Chinese, Norwegian, Swedish, Turkish or Vietnamese. That list is what AssemblyAI published on 2026-09-17, so it can fall behind.

## Reuse a transcript

Each media file's transcript is kept in the project package, every word as AssemblyAI sent it. A later run that wants the same transcript uses it, with no upload, no request and no cost.

A transcript is reused when all of these match:

- **The file:** its size, modified time and duration, and whether it has audio. Change the file, or relink to a different one, and it's transcribed again.
- **The model** Frame Job asks for.
- **The language:** **Detect automatically** and a named language count as different, as do two named languages.
- **Speakers:** on or off.
- **Vocabulary:** the same terms in the same order.

The caption style and the looks don't count, so [restyling](/captions/restyle-captions/) never uploads. Your region doesn't count either, so changing it uploads nothing again.

A transcript made for [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) serves captions too, as long as those settings match.

The transcript belongs to the media entry, not the file on disk. Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.

## Transcribe again

Tick **Transcribe again:** ("ignore any cached transcript") to ignore what's kept and ask AssemblyAI again. It's off by default. Each file goes up in full and is billed again, and the summary line shows that price.

Frame Job won't do this for a file with a [pending delete](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#a-pending-delete-holds-a-file-back) until the delete goes through.

## Generate with no key

With no key set, the note reads "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.", **Generate** is greyed, and resting the pointer on it shows the same sentence. Saving a key in Settings turns **Generate** on with the sheet still open.

The exception is work you've already paid for. When every file in the run has a current transcript, **Generate** works with no key, and the paragraph at the top changes to "Current cached transcripts will be used without an API key or network request." Ticking **Transcribe again:** ends that, because it needs a new upload.

With a key set the paragraph stays as it is, and the summary line says there's nothing to upload.

## Transcribe an untitled project

You don't have to save first. An untitled project's transcripts stay in a temporary folder and move into the project package on its first save. Close the project without saving and they're gone, so the same files would be paid for again in a new project.

In the rare case that a project has no folder for them at all, **Generate** is greyed and the note reads "This project has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it cannot be transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first."

## What the result says

While a run goes, the card's detail line shows the stage for each file: "Extracting", "Uploading" with the megabytes sent, "Submitting", "Waiting for AssemblyAI" with the seconds so far, and "Saving".

A run with nothing to report closes the sheet by itself. If there is something, the card stays open with **Close**, and these lines can join the usual count of captions added:

| The card says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "“interview.mov”: detected Spanish (97% confidence)." | With **Detect automatically**, the language AssemblyAI found in each file it just transcribed, and how sure it was. The figure is left out if AssemblyAI gave none. |
| "“interview.mov” was transcribed with universal-2, not universal-3-5-pro." | AssemblyAI used the fallback model. |
| "The transcript of “interview.mov” could not be kept in the project for reuse." | The captions are fine, but a later run may upload and bill this file again. |
| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of…" | See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-the-result-warns-about). |

## When a file fails

One file's failure doesn't end a run. Its clips are listed with the reason, and captions from the other files are still placed. If every file fails, nothing is placed and the card shows why.

Two things end a run early, and neither places anything: choosing **Cancel**, and a key AssemblyAI refuses, because every later upload would fail the same way. Files that had already finished stay in the project, so a later run doesn't pay for them again.

| The reason reads | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| "No network connection" | Frame Job couldn't reach AssemblyAI. |
| "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | AssemblyAI turned the key down, and the run stops there. Try **Verify** in [Settings](/captions/assemblyai-key/#verify). |
| "AssemblyAI answered 500" | AssemblyAI had a problem of its own. The number varies. |
| "AssemblyAI did not finish the transcript in the time allowed." | Frame Job waits at least 5 minutes for a transcript, and longer for audio over about 4 hours. |
| "“name” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file." | Nothing was sent for this file. |
| "AssemblyAI may have created a transcript, but Frame Job could not recover its ID…" | The answer to the request was lost. Check your AssemblyAI dashboard before you try again, because the transcript may still be there. |
| AssemblyAI's own sentence | AssemblyAI turned the request down or couldn't transcribe the file, perhaps over a problem with your account, and Frame Job passes on its words. |

A failed upload is tried once more, unless AssemblyAI turned it down outright. While waiting, Frame Job checks on the transcript every 3 seconds and rides out up to 3 failed checks in a row. It never follows a redirect, so your key can't reach another host, and the run reports that instead.

## Filler words stay out of captions

AssemblyAI's words include fillers, and captions leave them out, so a caption reads the same whether or not its transcript has them. The sheet's preview leaves them out too.

The words left out are um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er and erm, in any case and with any punctuation at their edges. The kept transcript still has them, which is what lets [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) find them later.

## With an agent

`transcribe` never picks this engine by itself: an agent has to ask for AssemblyAI on each call, whatever the sheet last chose. It can pass any language code, and one AssemblyAI doesn't support comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence after the upload.

The built-in [Assistant](/assistant/privacy/) can't use this engine at all. Your audio leaves the Mac only when you choose that in the sheet, with the price in front of you.

See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/)
- [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/)
- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
- [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/)
- [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/)

title: Re-lay captions for a canvas
description: Page word captions again after a canvas size change, keeping every word you corrected, and find out why a track was left as it was.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Word captions are paged for the canvas they were made on, so a narrower canvas can leave them too wide. Re-lay Captions pages them again for the new width, from the words they already hold.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas" tools="relay_captions" />

## Re-lay Captions for This Canvas

<Steps>

1. [Change the canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) on the Document tab.

2. Choose **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**. It has no keyboard shortcut and no options.

3. If a sheet appears, read which tracks were [kept as placed](#tracks-kept-as-placed) and why.

</Steps>

Frame Job looks at every track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips. A track whose pages are all in one of the five [word styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/), with the same [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/), is paged again from the words its pages hold. Nothing is transcribed again, so nothing is uploaded or billed.

The whole re-lay is one undo step, **Re-lay Captions**.

## What a re-lay keeps

Every correction you typed is kept, because the new pages are made from the words on the old ones.

Each page is paged again inside its own clip, and the new pages take the old track's place:

- A page you split, trimmed or moved keeps its words where they are.
- Pages are never merged across clips. A re-lay can split a page that's too wide for the new canvas, but a wider canvas won't join short pages together.
- Words cut off by a trim stay cut off.
- The new pages go on a track with the same name, in the same place in the track stack, hidden and locked if the old one was.

The new pages are drawn fresh from the style, so any other change you made to a page goes. That includes a colour, an outline, a size, a position, or an unticked **UPPERCASE**.

## Tracks kept as placed

A track that can't be re-laid stays exactly as it was. A sheet after the edit names each one and why, under a first line that reads "Re-laid 2 caption tracks for this canvas." or "No caption track was re-laid."

Each track gets a line like this:

> Caption track "Captions 2" is kept as placed: it holds a page with no word timings.

| The reason | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| it is a matte track | The track is a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/). |
| it holds a page with no word timings | It's a [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) or imported track, or a page lost its timing because you [changed its number of words](/captions/edit-captions/). |
| it holds a page none of whose words starts inside it | A trim or split left a page with no word that begins on it. |
| it holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make | You changed a page's font, or an agent changed its word style. |
| its pages are in more than one style | Pages on the track differ in style or looks, for example after you moved some from another track. |
| *N* captions is more than this project has room for | The new pages would take the project past its limit of 4,096 clips. The sentence says how many more would fit. |

No sheet appears when every track was re-laid.

To re-wrap a Subtitles track, or a track that lost its timing, generate it again on the new canvas. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).

## When it is available, and inside a nest

The item is greyed out when:

- there's no caption track it can re-lay
- a sheet is open
- a recording is running

So if every caption track would be kept as placed, the item is greyed out and no sheet tells you why. The table above lists what to look for.

Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), it works on the nest's tracks at the nest's size.

**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** does the same for the vertical copy. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).

## Good to know

- A track with any other name isn't looked at, and the sheet doesn't mention it. Neither is a track that holds a clip other than text.
- The item doesn't check whether the canvas changed. Choosing it on the same canvas pages the track again, which still drops the hand changes listed in [What a re-lay keeps](#what-a-re-lay-keeps). Undo brings them back.

## With an agent

`relay_captions` does the same in the timeline or nest that's open. When nothing can be re-laid, it answers with each kept track and its reason, so an agent can tell you why the menu item is greyed out. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/)
- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
- [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/)
- [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)

title: "Import captions"
description: "Bring a SubRip (.srt) caption file onto the timeline as text clips, and see what Frame Job copes with, removes and reports along the way."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Import Captions reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file onto a new caption track, one text clip per caption, as a single undo step. Use it when someone has already written the captions.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Import Captions…" tools="import_captions" />

## Import captions

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Import Captions…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it's available whenever the project window has no sheet open.

2. Pick the file. The open panel reads "Choose a SubRip (.srt) caption file." It accepts `.srt` and any plain-text file, so a SubRip file saved as `.txt` imports too.

</Steps>

Each caption becomes one text clip in the [**Caption** preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), on a new track at the front called **Captions**, or the next free number. Undo removes the lot in one step, **Import Captions**. With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, the track goes at the front of the nest.

A clean import shows no message. If there's anything to tell you, an alert appears when it finishes. See [Malformed entries are reported](#malformed-entries-are-reported).

A caption file comes in through this command, not as media. Frame Job can write WebVTT (`.vtt`) when you [export captions](/captions/export-captions/), but it has no reader for it.

## What the reader tolerates

Real SubRip files vary, and Frame Job copes with these variations rather than turning the file away:

- A UTF-8 byte-order mark.
- Windows (CRLF) or old Mac (bare CR) line endings.
- A missing index line above the timing line.
- A comma or a dot before the milliseconds.
- The `MM:SS` and `SS` shorthands, and up to nine digits after the seconds.
- Position settings after the end time, which are ignored.
- Text in UTF-8, UTF-16, Windows-1252 or Latin-1.

## What happens to the text

A text clip holds one plain string, so formatting that can't be kept is removed rather than shown as angle brackets on the canvas.

| In the file | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `<i>`, `<b>`, `<u>`, `<font …>` and their closing tags | Removed, along with anything else shaped like a tag: a `<` followed by a letter, or by `/` and a letter, up to the next `>`. |
| `{\an8}`-style overrides | Removed: a `{\` up to the next `}`. |
| `&` `<` `>` `"` `'` `'` ` ` | Decoded to the character they stand for. |
| Text that only looks like a tag, such as `<<` or `a < b` | Stays as text. |

The file's own line breaks are kept, and long lines also wrap inside the caption box, which is 80% of the canvas width.

## What happens to the timing

Every time snaps to the project's frame grid. A caption that starts before the previous one ends cuts the earlier one back to meet it. A caption left shorter than one frame is skipped. [Frame grid and no overlaps](/captions/how-captions-work/#frame-grid-and-no-overlaps) has the rules.

## Malformed entries are reported

Frame Job skips an entry it can't read, carries on with the rest, and tells you. Nothing is dropped silently.

When the import finishes with something to report, an alert headed "Imported 42 captions from “interview.srt”." says how many captions were shortened to fit and lists what was skipped by line number. It shows the first eight, then "…and N more."

| The alert says | What's wrong with the entry |
| --- | --- |
| no “-->” timing line in this entry | The block has no timing line. |
| “…” is not a HH:MM:SS,mmm time | A time can't be read. A time past 1,000,000 seconds, about 277 hours, counts as unreadable. |
| two “-->” in one timing line | The timing line has more than one arrow. |
| 2 lines before the timing line | More than an index line sits above the timing line. |
| ends at or before it starts | The end time isn't after the start time. |
| no caption text | The entry has timing but no words, or nothing left once markup is removed. |
| starts less than a frame before the next caption | Shortening it to fit would leave it under one frame. |

On a canvas taller than wide, the alert also says when captions wrap to more than two lines. See [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/).

## When a file can't be read

If not one caption in a file can be read, Frame Job imports nothing and the project doesn't change.

| The message says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| No captions could be read from “name.srt”. | Every entry failed. The message gives the first three reasons. |
| “name.srt” could not be read as text. | The file couldn't be opened. |
| “name.srt” holds 5000 captions, more than this project has room for: 900 more clips would fit, out of 4096. | The file would take the project past its 4,096-clip limit. |

## Good to know

The reader tries UTF-8, then UTF-16, then the two single-byte encodings. Latin-1 can read any byte, so a file in some other encoding still imports, but its accented letters may come out wrong. Convert it to UTF-8 and import it again.

## With an agent

`import_captions` can put the captions on a track that already exists, which the menu can't. Captions that would overlap something on that track are dropped, so leaving it to make a new track is the safer choice. It reports what landed and each malformed entry by line. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

title: "Export captions"
description: "Write a track of captions out as a SubRip or WebVTT file to ship beside your movie, without changing the project."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Export Captions writes one track of captions out as a separate subtitle file, for a platform or player that takes one. Burned-in captions need none of this: they're part of the picture in any [movie you export](/export/export-sheet/).

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export Captions…" tools="export_captions" />

## Export captions

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Export Captions…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it's greyed out until some track holds only text clips, with caption text on at least one of them.

2. In the save panel, choose the [**Track**](#track) and the [**Format**](#format-subrip-or-webvtt). The name starts as your project's name with `.srt` on the end.

3. Choose **Save**.

</Steps>

Exporting changes nothing in the project, so there's no undo step. If the file can't be written, an alert says why.

## Track

The **Track** pop-up lists the tracks you can write, front-most first, with the front-most chosen. Each row reads like "Captions — 12 cues (track 4)". The pop-up is greyed when there's only one to choose.

Nothing marks a track as a caption track, so any track made only of text clips is listed, a titles track included. A track with any other kind of clip on it isn't listed, and neither is one whose text clips are all empty.

With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the list shows that nest's tracks.

## Format: SubRip or WebVTT

The **Format** pop-up offers **SubRip (.srt)**, the default, and **WebVTT (.vtt)**. Choose whichever your player or platform asks for. Changing it changes the extension in the name field and keeps the name you've typed.

The words and times are the same in both. The files differ like this:

| | SubRip | WebVTT |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First line of the file | The first cue | `WEBVTT` |
| A number above each cue | Yes | No |
| Timestamps | `00:00:04,133` | `00:00:04.133` |
| `&`, `<` and `>` in the text | Written as they are | Escaped |

Both use LF line endings and end with one newline.

## One cue per text clip

Each text clip on the track becomes one cue, at the time and with the words it has now. A caption you dragged exports where you dragged it. Styling plays no part, so restyling a caption doesn't change the file.

- A caption with no text is left out.
- Line endings become LF. Blank lines inside a caption are removed, and so are spaces at the ends of its lines.
- A word caption track is written one cue per page, with the page's words as written. The style's **UPPERCASE**, the word timings and the styling don't go in the file.

## Frame-exact round trips

Export a track and [import it again](/captions/import-captions/), and every cue goes back on the frame it came from, at every ordinary frame rate.

The file itself may not match the one you first imported, because import snaps times to the frame grid. At 30 fps, `00:00:04,120` comes back as `00:00:04,133`. A file only comes back byte for byte when its cue times are already on the grid and a frame lasts a whole number of milliseconds, as it does at 25 or 50 fps.

## With an agent

`export_captions` never guesses the track. With no track to write, or with more than one and none named, it writes nothing and lists the candidates. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

Frame Job studies your files so its commands know where the cuts fall, who's in frame and when someone is talking. All of it happens on this Mac, with no upload, no network request and no key.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes', 'Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'Clip ▸ Remove Background', 'Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…']}
  where={['The Analyzing sheet', 'Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Background']}
  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'analyze_cutout', 'split_at_shots', 'reframe_clip', 'detect_silence', 'set_media_speech', 'set_video', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version']}
  needs="Nothing. Every analysis runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

This page explains the analysis itself. How to use a result is on the page of the feature that uses it.

## What Frame Job works out

| Result | When it's made | What uses it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Filmstrips, waveforms and loudness](#whats-built-when-a-file-arrives) | When a file arrives | The timeline and the audio tools |
| [Voice detection](#voice-detection) | When a file arrives | Remove Silences, Enhance Voice, Duck by Speech and others |
| [Shots](#shots) | When something asks | Split at Shot Changes, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version |
| [Faces](#faces) | When something asks | Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Switch by Speaker, Show Subjects |
| [People and salient regions](#people-and-salient-regions) | When something asks | Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Show Subjects |
| [Person masks](#person-masks) | When a clip needs them | Remove Background, Text Behind Subject |
| [Foreground masks](#foreground-masks-on-pictures) | When a picture needs one | Remove Background |
| [Sound events](#sound-events) | When an agent asks | Agents only |

## Analysis happens on demand

Importing a file doesn't analyse its picture. Frame Job does that when something asks for it: Split at Shot Changes, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Switch by Speaker, Remove Background or an agent.

Only the part that's needed is read:

- Follow Subject asks for the part of the file each clip plays.
- Split at Shot Changes reads the parts its clips play, and skips any stretch of the file between them that no clip uses.
- A part that's already been analysed isn't read again, so a second request over the same footage starts at once.

If two analyses of one file run at different times, what they find is added together. Neither replaces the other.

## The Analyzing sheet

When a menu command needs an analysis that isn't in the project yet, the **Analyzing** sheet comes up while it's made. When everything is already there, the sheet doesn't appear and the command goes straight ahead.

<Shot
  name="15f-analyzing-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Analyzing sheet for Split at Shot Changes. A sentence explains that nothing changes until the analysis is found and that Stop leaves everything as it is. Below it, the file speech.mov has an empty progress bar and the word Waiting, and a Stop button sits at the bottom right."
/>

The sheet has one row for each file that needs work, with its name, a bar and a status:

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Waiting | Frame Job hasn't read the file's first frame yet. |
| A percentage | The share of the work done so far. |
| Done | This file has finished. |

For [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/), a file can have a row for each thing being found, such as "speech.mov — Faces", "speech.mov — Shot changes" and "speech.mov — People and salient regions".

These commands use the sheet:

- **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**
- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**, after you press **Follow** in its own sheet
- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**, after you press **Make** in its own sheet
- **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**, before its own sheet, when it needs to find faces because it's working from one microphone

When every row is done, the sheet closes by itself and the command carries on. Every editor action is off while the sheet is up.

If the project changes while the sheet is up, which an agent can do, the command makes no edit. The inspector says so and asks you to choose the command again.

[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) doesn't use this sheet. It makes its masks while you go on working, and shows its progress in **Status** in the Clip tab's **Background** section.

### Stop an analysis

Choose **Stop**, or press <kbd>Esc</kbd>. The sheet closes, the command is cancelled and no edit is made. What was already saved stays in the project, so choosing the command again carries on from there.

Minimising the window also stops the work. When you bring the window back, the sheet starts again on whatever hadn't finished.

### When an analysis fails

If an analysis can't finish, the command stops instead of editing with half an answer. Frame Job beeps, and the foot of the inspector names the file and the reason, for example: "The shots analysis of “interview.mov” failed: …"

If a file is missing or can't be read, the command stops before the sheet opens. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).

## Analysis runs in the background

You can keep working while an analysis runs, except while the Analyzing sheet is up.

- Picture analysis runs at low priority, one job at a time across all your open projects.
- Sound analysis has its own queue, so one sound job can run beside one picture job.
- Frame Job saves what it has found every 30 seconds, and at the end of each stretch of the file it reads. If a job stops part-way, everything saved so far is kept and the next request continues from there.
- A job that nothing wants any more is dropped if it hasn't started, and cancelled if it has. Closing a project does this to its jobs.

## What each analysis finds

### Shots

Frame Job finds the hard cuts in a video by comparing each frame's colours with the frames before it. This is plain arithmetic, with no machine learning.

- A gradual dissolve isn't reported as a cut.
- A single flash frame isn't a cut.
- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can show as one cut.

[Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/) cuts your clips at these moments.

### Faces

Frame Job looks for faces ten times a second of the file's own time, using Apple's Vision framework. For each face it keeps its box, how far it's turned and tilted, and how open the mouth is.

Faces are listed from left to right. They carry no identity, so Frame Job doesn't know that a face in one sample is the same person in the next, and it never puts names to faces.

### People and salient regions

At the same ten samples a second, Frame Job finds:

- **People**, as a box around each person's head and shoulders.
- **Salient regions**, as boxes around the parts of the picture the eye goes to first. In a talking-head shot this is usually the speaker. On a slide it's often the text.

Each sample is judged on its own, so no person is followed from one moment to the next. See [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/) for how Frame Job uses them, and [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) to see faces, people and salient regions over the preview.

### Person masks

A person mask is an outline of a person, made for every frame of the video that a clip plays. [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) and [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) draw with these masks, and they're made when a clip has one of those on.

A frame counts as holding a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half strength. The masks are kept at the size Vision makes them, one for every frame, so a long clip's masks take up room in the package.

### Foreground masks on pictures

On a still picture, Frame Job can mask the foreground subject, whether or not it's a person. Turn on Remove Background, then choose **Foreground** in the **Subject** row of the Clip tab's **Background** section. The row appears when every selected clip is a picture, and **Person** is the default.

Either way a picture gets one mask, made from the picture as it's drawn, the right way up.

### Sound events

Frame Job can listen to a file's first sound track and score how likely six kinds of sound are: laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech. It uses Apple's Sound Analysis, in overlapping windows 1.5 seconds long that start every 0.75 seconds. Each score runs from 0 to 1, and there's no score where a window runs past the end of the sound.

Only an agent can ask for these, and no menu or pane uses them. Treat the scores as hints, never as a finding on their own, because they haven't been checked against recordings with known sounds.

The file needs sound, and an audio file works. Frame Job won't read sound events for a clip that plays in reverse, because its sound runs backwards.

## What's built when a file arrives

After you open a project, import a file or relink one, Frame Job builds these in the background, and the timeline fills in as they finish:

- **Filmstrip thumbnails** for clips on the timeline. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
- **The waveform**, at 100 peaks a second.
- **The loudness record**, in 10 ms steps, which Normalize, Enhance Voice and the loudness read-outs use.
- **Sound-matching features**, which [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) uses.
- **[Voice detection](#voice-detection)**.

At most two files' sound is read at a time, so a big import doesn't hold up playback or a speed ramp's sound. A cache that already matches its file is never rebuilt. A file with no sound has no waveform, loudness or voice detection, and a `.cube` LUT file gets none of these.

Until a cache lands, the controls that need it wait or read "measuring…". A command that needs it says the file is still being analysed and asks you to try again in a moment.

If a waveform or loudness pass fails, Frame Job tries again after 2 seconds and again after 10. After that it tries the next time you open the project.

### Voice detection

Frame Job scores every 32 ms of a file's sound for speech, using the Silero voice model bundled with the app. That's how later commands tell a voice from noise. These use it:

- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/voice-or-level/), in its **Voice** mode
- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/)
- The [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
- [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/)
- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)
- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/) and [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/)

If the voice model can't be used, Remove Silences says so and judges quiet by level instead.

## Results are kept per file

Anything Frame Job finds is kept for the file, not for a clip, in the project's cache. Every clip of a file shares it, and a second request over the same part answers at once. Picture analysis and sound events live in the `.framejob` package under `cache/analysis/`.

A result counts only for the file it was made from, which Frame Job checks by the file's size, modification time and length. Relink a clip to a different file, or change the file on disk, and it's analysed again. An unchanged file isn't.

Picture analysis and sound events also record the macOS build they were made on. After a macOS update, or on a Mac running a different build, they're made again the next time something asks.

## Results travel with the project

The caches live inside the `.framejob` package, so they go wherever it goes. Moving, copying or consolidating a package keeps them. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/) for what's inside.

A new project made from this one starts with them too, so nothing is analysed twice. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) and the **Make a copy** option of [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) carry these, for each file the new project keeps:

- Filmstrips, waveforms and loudness
- Voice detection and sound-matching features
- On-device transcripts
- Everything on this page that's found in the picture or sound
- The reversed render of any clip that plays backwards

Your media files are never copied. Neither is speed-ramp audio, or a voice-isolated or voice-effect render, and those are made again when they're needed. A cloud transcript stays behind unless its copy on AssemblyAI has already been deleted.

## Good to know

- **Show Subjects** never starts an analysis. Where nothing has been found it reads "Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it".
- A package with a missing or damaged cache still opens and redraws. Picture analysis is made again when something next asks, but a lost cloud transcript costs money to make again.
- Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches sit in a temporary folder. The first save copies them into the package.

## With an agent

An agent can read the results themselves with `get_media_analysis`, for a whole file or for the part one clip plays, and it's the only way to reach [sound events](#sound-events). It shows no sheet. It waits at most 60 seconds, then stops and says how much it covered. What it covered is kept, so asking again carries on.

`analyze_cutout` makes a clip's masks and says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

Masks are made on this Mac with Vision's person segmentation at its balanced setting. Nothing is uploaded, and no key is needed. They're kept per media in the project's cache, so a frame that's been analysed is never analysed again. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#person-masks).

Until a frame has its mask, the clip draws whole in the preview. A paused frame redraws by itself as masks land, and a playing preview picks them up on its next frame.

### Status

**Status** says where the clip's masks stand, and why a clip is drawing whole.

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Analyzing N %** | The masks are being made. The figure stops at 99 until they're done. |
| **Ready** | Every frame the clip plays has its mask. |
| **No person found** | Every frame was looked at and no person is in the clip, so it draws whole. A frame counts as holding a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half. |
| **No subject found** | A picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground** was looked at and no subject was found, so it draws whole. |
| **Failed:** and the reason | The masks couldn't be made. The media file may be missing or unreadable, or the masks couldn't be written. Fix the cause and choose **Analyze Now**. |
| **No picture to analyze** | The clip plays no frame of its file. |
| **Off** | Remove Background is off. |
| **—** | Several clips are selected. The section's header then reads "on". |

### Analyze Now

**Analyze Now** asks again for the masks the clip needs, then retries a run that failed. It's enabled only while a clip is analysing or has failed.

## Pictures

<Shot
  name="05k-clip-background-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Background section for an image clip. Remove background is ticked, a Subject row reads Foreground above Background, which reads Remove, then Edge, Feather and a Status of Analyzing 0 %."
/>

A picture gets one mask, made once on this Mac from the picture as the preview draws it, the right way up. Because it's one frame, **Status** goes straight from Analyzing to **Ready**.

**Person** uses the same person segmentation as a video. **Foreground** uses Vision's foreground instance mask, which keeps every foreground subject it finds. If it finds none, **Status** reads **No subject found** and the picture draws whole.

## Exports

An export draws the subject alone in every frame, GIF and APNG included. It waits at "Preparing…" until every mask it draws is made, with no time limit, and you can cancel it while it waits.

If a mask can't be made, the export fails with "Clip n's person masks could not be made: …" and writes no file. For a picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground**, the message says "foreground masks".

A single frame doesn't wait as long. **File ▸ Save Frame…** (<kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>) waits up to 30 seconds for the masks it needs. If they aren't ready by then, it saves the frame with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the files drawn whole. An agent's [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) waits the same 30 seconds and says so in its answer.

## Good to know

- A clip draws whole only when no frame it plays has a person. If the person leaves the picture for part of a clip, those frames have little or nothing to keep, so what's behind shows through.
- The recorder panel can do this for you. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## With an agent

An agent turns this on with `set_video`, as the checkbox does. `analyze_cutout` can wait up to 60 seconds for a clip's masks to settle, and it answers the subject's mean centre in the picture, which the app doesn't show. For a video, `get_media_analysis` says which stretches of the file hold a person. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

## AssemblyAI first, otherwise this Mac

For each file, the tab takes the first of these it finds:

1. **An AssemblyAI transcript.** You have one if you've used [**File ▸ Generate Captions…** with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) or [**Remove Filler Words**](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) on the file. Using it needs no key.
2. **A reading on this Mac.** Otherwise the tab transcribes the file the first time you look, in your Mac's language unless you [choose another](/captions/transcript-tab/#language).

Reading on this Mac is quick: about 0.7 seconds a minute of speech on an M2 Max, so an hour takes well under a minute. Playback keeps running while it reads.

The tab never makes a network request, whichever source it uses.

## One file at a time, playhead first

Files are read one at a time, starting with the one under the playhead. Each file's words appear as soon as it's done, without waiting for the rest.

If you switch to another tab, the reading stops, and it picks up when you come back. To stop it yourself, use [**Stop**](/captions/transcript-tab/#read-and-stop).

## Kept per file and language

What this Mac heard is kept in the project, one reading for each file and language, so the next look is immediate.

Each file is read whole, once. Trimming a clip, adding another clip of the same file or changing its speed doesn't read it again.

A reading is used only while the file and the macOS version are the same. If either changes, or you choose another language, the file is read again.

These readings are only for the transcript. [Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) never use them.

## When no speech model is installed

If your Mac has no speech model, the tab says:

> This Mac has no speech model installed. Choose File ▸ Generate Captions…, pick a language and press Download.

Do that, then come back to the tab. A file with an AssemblyAI transcript shows its words in the meantime.

A file this Mac can't read is named in the same place, and the tab carries on with the others. It tries that file again when you next come back to the tab.

## Ramped clips and following edits

Words are placed through a clip's speed, including a [ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), so a word's time matches what plays on the timeline.

Editing the timeline updates the text right away, and the words you were reading stay where they were. During a drag, the text updates when you let go.

## With an agent

When an agent reads a file on this Mac, the tab's **Stop** leaves that reading running. The Assistant's own **Stop** ends it, and nothing is saved from a stopped reading. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

| **Karaoke** | Yellow | White at 55% |
| **Build** | Yellow | Not drawn yet |

**Pill** and **One Word** can't use this look, because their spoken word is the same colour on both sides of the fill.

## Dim in pauses

The page fades to half opacity during a pause of 0.25 s or more, then comes back before the next word. Each fade takes 0.1 s, and the words and the pill fade together. It works with all five word styles.

The page also dims:

- before the first word, when that word starts late. The page opens dim, with no fade.
- after the last word, until the caption ends.

A pause of 0.25 s also [ends a page](/captions/word-caption-styles/#where-a-page-breaks), so on a generated track you'll mostly see the dim at the end of a page, after its last word.

With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style selected, a note under the boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI." The on-device recogniser stretches each word's time across the silence after it, so few pauses are long enough to dim.

The sheet's [preview](/captions/word-caption-styles/#the-sheets-two-frame-preview) doesn't show this look.

## Word colours

The inspector has no section for a page's word colours, pop size or pill. Nothing in the Clip tab changes the yellow, the violet or how far the word pops.

To change them, generate again with a [different style](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again), or have an agent do it.

The **Color** row under **Text ▸ Style** still works on the words drawn in the text's own colour. That's the white words in **Highlight** and **Build**, and every word in **Pill** and **One Word**. It leaves the yellow alone, and it changes nothing in **Karaoke**, which sets all its own colours.

## With an agent

An agent can do two things here that the sheet can't.

It can change a placed page's word style with `set_text`. That covers highlighting or building word by word, the colours of the spoken word and of the words before and after it, a pop from 100% to 150%, the pill's colour, padding and corners, and how far the page dims, from none to fully invisible. The sheet's dim is always half. A page changed this way is no longer one of the styles Frame Job makes, so [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed) keeps its track as placed. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

It can also ask for looks with `transcribe`, but each one is off unless it asks, never what the sheet last chose. Frame Job won't add a look to a style it wouldn't show on. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

2. Open the **Clip** tab and its **Text** sub-tab.

## Good to know

- **Replace:** always opens unticked. The sheet doesn't remember it.
- A hidden or locked caption track is replaced like any other, and the new track is visible and unlocked.
- If you cancel a run, nothing is placed and the old tracks stay.
- If one file can't be transcribed, the captions from the other files are still placed and the old tracks still go, so the captions over that file's clips are lost. Undo brings them back.
- To go from a word style back to Subtitles, generate the Subtitles track, then [remove the old one](/timeline/manage-tracks/). **Replace:** isn't available for that.
- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the sheet works on that nest's tracks.

## With an agent

`transcribe` restyles the same way, as long as it asks for a word style and places the captions. An agent can also change a placed page's word style directly with `set_text`, which keeps your corrected words. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#with-an-agent).
